name: the Orient restates the reading's happened_at contract
old: A reading's happened_at.source is its cited row's n; happened_at.expression copies that row's own time words or is null when there are none. Its send timestamp is not its event time: code resolves the quoted expression. Record unknown event time honestly.
new: Record a reading using its send timestamp as event time.

name: the repair rule replaces retry-only coverage
old: repair the rejected field of each still-grounded statement, preserving its meaning, mode and citations
new: retry only the items not already covered

name: the Act date rule is scoped away from happened_at
old: Notebook, event and reminder date fields use dates and clock times grounded in the supplied clock, not relative words; memory's quoted happened_at expression has its own meaning above.
new: All date fields, including memory happened_at, use absolute dates instead of relative words.

name: the uncomprehended item is not threatened with striking out
new: An uncomprehended item consumes a return attempt.

name: happened_at carries its quote-or-null description into the schema
old:
expression: str | None = Field(default=None, description=(
        "The exact time words copied from that row's body — «tomorrow», «on "
        "Saturday» — or null when the row states none. Never the row's `at` "
        "metadata and never a date you computed: code resolves the quoted "
        "words against that row's send time. The only nullable field here."))

name: a refused statement carries its field and repair
the primary refusal list carries field, repair and cites
new:
{"statement": index, "kind": entry["kind"], "reason": entry["reason"]}
            for index, entry in report.items() if entry["status"] == "refused"

name: a reading drop is legible in the refused list
a malformed cite container never raises over saved siblings
old:
cites = raw.get("cite")
            if not isinstance(cites, (list, tuple)):
